title: Part
spec: Create a symmetrical, flat, rectangular shape with rounded corners by following these detailed steps. First, establish a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees around the x-axis, zero degrees around the y-axis, and negative ninety degrees around the z-axis. The translation vector should be set to zero for all axes. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. This sketch consists of a loop made up of eight lines. The first line starts at the origin and ends at zero point zero, zero point zero three seven five. The second line extends from this point to zero point one zero three one, zero point one eight seven five. The third line continues to zero point six four six nine, zero point one eight seven five. The fourth line moves to zero point seven five, zero point zero three seven five. The fifth line goes down to zero point seven five, zero point zero. The sixth line then slopes to zero point five four three eight, zero point one five four seven. The seventh line runs parallel to the x-axis to zero point two zero six two, zero point one five four seven. Finally, the eighth line returns to the origin. After completing the sketch, apply a scaling factor of zero point seven five to the entire sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it with the same Euler angles used in the coordinate system setup and translating it with the same vector. To finalize the model, extrude the transformed sketch zero point zero zero two eight units along the normal direction. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction of the normal. This process will create a new solid body with a length of zero point seven five units, a width of zero point one eight seven five units, and a height of zero point zero zero two eight units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0375) \
     .lineTo(0.1031, 0.1875) \
     .lineTo(0.6469, 0.1875) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0375) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.5438, 0.1547) \
     .lineTo(0.2062, 0.1547) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0028)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, so we need to use rotation matrices
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch points
points = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (0.0, 0.0375),
    (0.1125, 0.15),
    (0.1875, 0.15),
    (0.5625, 0.15),
    (0.6375, 0.15),
    (0.75, 0.0375),
    (0.75, 0.0),
    (0.6375, 0.1125),
    (0.5625, 0.1125),
    (0.1875, 0.1125),
    (0.1125, 0.1125),
    (0.0, 0.0)
]

# Create the sketch
r = r.polyline(points).close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0028)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, so we need to use rotation matrices
# The given Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) which corresponds to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

profile_pts = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (0.104, 0.1875),
    (0.635, 0.1875),
    (0.75, 0.0),
    (0.534, 0.149),
    (0.197, 0.149),
]

r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(*profile_pts[0])
    .lineTo(*profile_pts[1])
    .lineTo(*profile_pts[2])
    .lineTo(*profile_pts[3])
    .lineTo(*profile_pts[4])
